chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When ten years come upon the boy, it is allowed for him with regards to his wealth, what he emancipates, gives in charity, and bequeaths, upon a known limit and right, so it is valid.

key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: boy (specifically referring to a male child who has not yet reached full maturity/puberty in this context)
key_terms.حَدٍّ مَعْرُوفٍ: known limit (referring to the permissible portion of wealth one can dispose of, often one-third or the whole for a child depending on the school)
key_terms.عَشْرُ سِنِينَ: ten years (the specific age of legal capacity for financial transactions)

ai.seo_question: What are the financial legal capacities of a boy who has reached ten years of age in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the threshold of partial legal capacity (bulugh al-hukm) for a boy at age ten, distinguishing it from full maturity. It validates his discretionary disposal of wealth through emancipation, charity, and bequest, provided these acts conform to established Islamic limits and rights, reflecting the Shia juristic view that ten is the age of discernment for financial transactions.
